steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Definitions: Statistical (rare, e.g. IQ<70), Social norms (culture-specific), FFAD (distress, dysfunction), Ideal MH (Jahoda: autonomy, reality perception, etc.)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Phobias: Two-process (classical: fear acquisition, operant: avoidance maintenance); Preparedness (Seligman: evolved fears); CBT: exposure, cognitive restructuring

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Depression: Biological (5-HTT gene, serotonin, cortisol/HPA axis); Cognitive (Beck: negative triad, schema, cognitive distortions); Learned helplessness (Seligman); Treatments: SSRIs (6-8 weeks), CBT (behavioural activation, cognitive restructuring)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: OCD: Obsessions (intrusive), Compulsions (repetitive); Biological (COMT, SLC1A1, basal ganglia, serotonin); Cognitive (inflated responsibility, thought-action fusion); ERP (exposure response prevention)

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: Explain the two-process model of phobias and evaluate it --- Solution: Classical: neutral stimulus (spider) paired with fear (trauma) -> CS elicits CR (fear). Operant: avoidance reduces fear -> negative reinforcement maintains phobia. Evaluation: explains acquisition/maintenance; ignores cognition (irrational thoughts), preparedness (why spiders not flowers?), individual differences; CBT addresses limitations
